subtitle: The complete guide to keeping your engine running at peak performance past 60 000 km
problemHeadline: Is your car due for a major service?
problemBody: Every 60 000 km or 3 years your vehicle needs more than an oil change. A major service replaces filters, fluids, spark plugs and drive belts. Skipping it leads to premature engine wear, reduced fuel economy, and lower resale value.

pirbStandard: MIWA (Motor Industry Workshop Association) Code of Conduct; SANS 10100-1 for engine servicing

articleSections.heading: When does your car need a major service?
articleSections.body: Most manufacturers schedule a major service every 60 000 km or 36 months, whichever comes first. Turbo engines and cars driven in severe conditions — SA dusty gravel roads, Gauteng traffic, Durban coastal humidity — need earlier intervals. Your owner manual has the exact schedule.

articleSections.heading: What gets replaced during a major service?
articleSections.body: A major service covers everything a minor service does plus spark plugs (copper or iridium), fuel filter, cabin air filter, drive belt inspection, coolant flush, brake fluid flush, and sometimes transmission fluid. The mechanic also adjusts valve clearances on engines that need them. All fluids topped to manufacturer spec.

articleSections.heading: Why OEM parts matter
articleSections.body: Aftermarket parts save money upfront but fail faster. SA has a counterfeit auto parts market — fake oil filters disintegrate and clog galleries. SABS-approved OEM-equivalent parts from Bosch, NGK, or Febi Bilstein meet the same standards. Bouul mechanics use genuine or certified equivalent parts only.

articleSections.heading: The 72-point inspection explained
articleSections.body: Beyond service items, the mechanic checks tyres, brake pads and discs, suspension bushes, ball joints, CV boots, exhaust mounts, battery CCA, air-con gas pressure, wiper blades, and lights. Each item is marked pass/fail in your Bouul report so you know what needs attention next.

articleSections.heading: Average pricing in South Africa (2026)
articleSections.body: 4-cylinder sedan (Corolla, Polo, i20): R2 800–R5 500. 6-cylinder (BMW 3 Series, Audi A4, C-Class): R4 500–R8 500. V8 or luxury SUV (X5, GLE, Range Rover): R6 500–R12 000. Includes parts, labour, and digital inspection. Dealerships charge 40–60% more.

articleSections.heading: How Bouul protects you
articleSections.body: Bouul connects you with RMI-registered mobile mechanics who come to your home or office. You approve the parts list before work starts. Payment stays in escrow until you confirm satisfaction. If work isn't up to standard, Bouul mediates under MIWA dispute resolution.

title: Brake Pads: When to Replace and What to Expect
subtitle: Squeaking, grinding, or a soft pedal — know the signs before it costs you a rotor
problemHeadline: Your brake pads are wearing thin. What now?
problemBody: Brake pads last 30 000–65 000 km depending on driving style. Heavy SA stop-start traffic can cut that to 20 000 km. When pads wear past 3 mm, stopping distance increases and metal-on-metal contact destroys your discs.
bouulSolution: A Bouul mobile mechanic brings your exact pad set (semi-metallic or ceramic) and checks rotor thickness on arrival
They measure runout, lubricate slider pins, and bleed the system — not just swap pads and go
Bouul escrow holds payment until you confirm the pedal feels firm with no squeal on test drive
partsNeeded: Brake pads (front and/or rear set, semi-metallic or ceramic per manufacturer spec)
Brake discs (skim or replace if below minimum thickness)
Brake fluid (DOT 4 or DOT 5.1 per manufacturer)
Copper grease and brake cleaner
guidePricing: R800 – R2 200 per axle (pads only); R2 500 – R6 000 per axle (pads + discs)
aiPromptExample: 2017 VW Polo 1.0 TSI. Front brakes squeak when stopping. Pads checked 10 000 km ago at 4 mm. Worth buying ceramic for less dust?
aiDiagnosisOutput: 2017 Polo 1.0 TSI — front brake squeal. Likely worn pads below 3 mm or glazed surface. Fit ceramic pads (Ferodo or ATE) for reduced dust. Est. R1 200–R1 800 per axle.
escrowGuarantee: Your payment sits in Bouul escrow. Test the brakes — if you hear squealing after 200 km, we hold funds until the issue is fixed.
pirbStandard: RMI Brake Service Code of Practice; SANS 20053 brake system performance

articleSections.heading: When should you replace brake pads?
articleSections.body: The golden rule: replace pads at 3 mm remaining thickness. Many pads have a wear indicator that chirps when braking. Other signs: grinding (metal on metal), soft or spongey pedal (air in lines), or the car pulling to one side under braking (sticking caliper or uneven wear).

articleSections.heading: Semi-metallic vs ceramic pads for SA
articleSections.body: Semi-metallic pads are standard for most SA cars — they handle heat well and last longer but produce more dust. Ceramic pads run cleaner and quieter — ideal for luxury sedans with alloy wheels — but need more heat before they bite, less ideal for cold city stops.

articleSections.heading: Can you drive with worn pads?
articleSections.body: Technically yes but unsafe and expensive. Worn pads mean longer stopping distances — critical on SA highways. Once pads wear to the backing plate, the metal grinds grooves into your discs, turning a R1 500 job into R5 000+ with new discs.

articleSections.heading: What else should be done during a pad replacement?
articleSections.body: A proper brake job includes: measuring rotor thickness and runout, cleaning and greasing caliper slider pins, inspecting brake hoses, checking the handbrake mechanism, and flushing old brake fluid. Brake fluid is hygroscopic — in SA heat, old fluid can boil, causing sudden brake fade on descents like Van Reenen's Pass.

articleSections.heading: Average brake service pricing in SA (2026)
articleSections.body: Pads per axle — R800 to R2 200. Pads plus discs — R2 500 to R6 000 per axle. Brake fluid flush — R350 to R600. Caliper rebuild — R1 200 to R2 500 per corner. Most Bouul mechanics discount when doing both axles.

articleSections.heading: RMI compliance and your safety
articleSections.body: RMI-accredited mechanics follow the RMI Brake Service Code of Practice, mandating measurement documentation for every component. Your Bouul mechanic records all measurements — pad and rotor thickness, fluid condition. You get a digital copy for your service history.

title: Clutch Replacement: Cost, Symptoms, and How to Avoid a Gearbox Tear-Down
subtitle: That slipping clutch is only getting worse — here is what a replacement really involves
problemHeadline: Is your clutch on the way out?
problemBody: A clutch typically lasts 80 000–150 000 km. Heavy traffic in Sandton or Centurion accelerates wear. Symptoms: engine revs but speed does not follow (slipping), high biting point, difficulty engaging gears, or a burning smell. Ignoring these can damage the dual-mass flywheel, adding R5 000+ to the bill.
bouulSolution: Bouul vets mechanics with proven clutch experience on your specific make — some need special alignment tools
Your mechanic replaces the full kit (plate, pressure plate, release bearing) and inspects the flywheel while the gearbox is out
Escrow holds your payment until you test-drive and confirm smooth gear engagement across all ratios
partsNeeded: Clutch kit (plate, pressure plate, release bearing — Sachs, Valeo, or LUK recommended)
Dual-mass flywheel (inspect; replace if excessive play or hot spots)
Gearbox oil (MTF per manufacturer spec, e.g. 75W-80 for most FWD cars)
Pilot bearing and alignment tool (specific to engine/gearbox combination)
aiPromptExample: 2005 BMW 320d E90 manual. Clutch slips in 3rd and 4th above 2 500 rpm. Vibration when pulling away. Quoted R16 000 by BMW Midrand.
aiDiagnosisOutput: BMW 320d E90 — slipping clutch + vibration. Likely worn plate and failed DMF. Full clutch kit + DMF, gearbox oil. Est. R10 000–R14 000 (Sachs kit, independent).
escrowGuarantee: Your funds held in Bouul escrow. Full test drive through all gears including reverse before releasing. If gears crunch or clutch judders, payment stays frozen.
pirbStandard: RMI Drivetrain Code of Practice; SABS 1518 clutch assembly standards

articleSections.heading: How to tell your clutch is failing
articleSections.body: Classic symptom: revs rise but acceleration doesn't match — clutch is slipping. Other clues: very high biting point (worn friction plate), spongey pedal (hydraulic issue), rattle when idling in neutral (release bearing), or clutch judder when pulling away (flywheel glazed).

articleSections.heading: Clutch kit vs full replacement
articleSections.body: A clutch kit includes the plate, pressure plate, and release bearing. Replacing all three simultaneously is recommended because they wear as a set. If the flywheel shows heat damage, scoring, or excessive play, replace or resurface it — especially on DMF-equipped cars common in SA like VW Golf, Ford Ranger, and BMW 3 Series.

articleSections.heading: Why dual-mass flywheels are expensive
articleSections.body: Many modern SA cars use DMFs to dampen vibrations. DMFs have internal springs that wear. A failed DMF causes rattle at idle and vibration through the pedal. Replacing adds R4 000–R8 000 because the part is costly and the gearbox must come out anyway.

articleSections.heading: Choosing the right parts brand
articleSections.body: Sachs, Valeo, and LUK are OEM manufacturers for most European and Asian cars sold in SA. Counterfeit clutches are known — a fake Sachs kit may delaminate within 10 000 km. Bouul mechanics use verified supply chains with proof of purchase.

articleSections.heading: Average clutch costs in SA (2026)
articleSections.body: Entry FWD (Etios, Swift, Grand i10): R5 500–R8 500. Mid FWD (Corolla, Polo, Civic): R7 000–R12 000. RWD/SUV (3 Series, Ranger, Hilux): R9 000–R18 000. Includes labour, full kit, gearbox oil, workmanship warranty.

articleSections.heading: Extending clutch life in SA traffic
articleSections.body: The number one clutch killer is creeping in heavy traffic. Resting your foot on the pedal keeps the release bearing spinning. Hold the clutch at bite point as briefly as possible — use the handbrake on hills and leave space to roll instead of slipping the clutch repeatedly.

title: Timing Belt Replacement: The One Job You Cannot Afford to Skip
subtitle: Snapped timing belt = bent valves. Here is how to prevent a R25 000 engine rebuild.
problemHeadline: When was your timing belt last changed?
problemBody: The timing belt synchronises camshaft and crankshaft. Replacement is every 90 000 km or 5 years — but many SA cars are overdue. If the belt snaps on an interference engine (most modern cars), pistons hit valves, requiring a full head rebuild costing R15 000–R35 000.
bouulSolution: Bouul mechanics bring genuine timing belt kits including the tensioner, idler pulleys, and water pump
They follow manufacturer torque specs and alignment marks — no shortcuts, no guesswork
Escrow holds payment until you confirm the engine starts cleanly with no warning lights or unusual noises
partsNeeded: Timing belt (Gates, ContiTech, or Dayco — OEM supplier brands)
Tensioner assembly (hydraulic or mechanical per engine type)
Idler pulleys (replace with belt — failed pulleys snap new belts)
Water pump (driven off timing belt — replace proactively while access is free)
aiPromptExample: 2013 Ford Focus 1.6 Trend with 105 000 km. Not sure if belt was ever done. Quoted R8 200 by Ford East Rand. Fair for an independent?
aiDiagnosisOutput: 2013 Focus 1.6L — timing belt overdue (105k km, rec 90k/5yr). Interference engine — snap = bent valves. Full kit + water pump. Est. independent R4 500–R6 500. Dealer R7 000–R9 000.
escrowGuarantee: Bouul escrow holds your payment. After the job, start the engine and let it idle for 5 minutes. No ticking, no misfire, no check engine light? Release funds.
pirbStandard: MIWA Service Standards; SANS 20038 for engine timing systems

articleSections.heading: Timing belt vs timing chain
articleSections.body: Chains are theoretically lifetime but can stretch on neglected oil changes. Belts need proactive replacement. If your car has a belt (most VW 1.4/1.8 TSI, Ford 1.6/2.0, Toyota 1.8/2.0/2.4 petrol, most diesels), the interval is non-negotiable.

articleSections.heading: Why always replace the water pump?
articleSections.body: The water pump on many engines is driven by the timing belt. Replacing the belt without the pump saves R500 now but if the pump fails 20 000 km later, you pay full labour again. Water pump seal failure is common in hot SA climates.

articleSections.heading: What happens when a timing belt snaps?
articleSections.body: On an interference engine (most petrol and all diesel engines), pistons smash into open valves, bending them. Fix: cylinder head removal, valve replacement, often piston damage. Total: R15 000–R35 000.

articleSections.heading: Signs your timing belt needs urgent replacement
articleSections.body: Visible cracking, fraying on edges, or glazing. Ticking from timing cover (worn tensioner), low rumble (failing water pump bearing). Chirping sound at idle. Most belts fail without warning.

articleSections.heading: Is a dealership necessarily better?
articleSections.body: Dealerships charge 40–70% more than quality independents using the same OEM-spec parts. Ford East Rand quoted R8 200 for a Focus belt; an RMI independent with genuine Ford kit would charge R4 500–R5 500.

articleSections.heading: After replacement: what to watch for
articleSections.body: Smooth idle with no ticking or whirring from the timing cover. Check engine light stays off after 20 km. Some cars need ignition timing re-adapted. Bouul mechanics include a follow-up scan at no extra cost.

title: Gearbox Replacement: Manual or Auto, Know Your Options
subtitle: A failing gearbox does not always mean a full replacement — but when it does, you need this guide
problemHeadline: Your gearbox is failing. What is the real cost?
problemBody: Gearbox failure symptoms: grinding gears (manual), delayed engagement (auto), slipping between gears, whining noises in neutral. A full replacement is the most expensive single repair on most cars. Sometimes a rebuild or used unit is viable. SA gearbox specialists in Germiston and Cape Town can rebuild units for half new cost.
bouulSolution: Bouul connects you with gearbox specialists who diagnose via computer scan before recommending replacement vs rebuild
Your mechanic provides a detailed quote with three options: rebuild, refurbished unit, or new OEM
Escrow ensures you only pay when the gearbox shifts smoothly through every gear under all driving conditions
partsNeeded: Gearbox unit (new OEM, refurbished exchange, or used low-km — ZF, Aisin, Getrag)
Clutch kit (manual — replace clutch while gearbox is out)
Gearbox oil and filter (ATF for automatics, MTF for manuals)
Input shaft seal, output shaft seal, and gasket set
guidePricing: R8 000 – R18 000 (manual rebuild/exchange); R15 000 – R35 000 (automatic rebuild/exchange)
aiPromptExample: 2010 Audi A4 2.0 TDI Multitronic. Transmission jerks in traffic and will not select reverse sometimes. Audi Zwartkops quoted R42 000 for new gearbox.
aiDiagnosisOutput: 2010 A4 2.0 TDI CVT — jerking + reverse failure. Likely valve body or mechatronic unit. CVT rebuild feasible at specialist R18 000–R28 000 vs R42 000 new.
escrowGuarantee: Bouul holds payment until you complete a 50 km test drive covering highway, traffic, hill starts, and reverse. Any hesitation or shudder means the mechanic fixes it.
pirbStandard: RMI Transmission Code of Practice; SANS 20062 gearbox performance testing

articleSections.heading: Manual vs automatic gearbox failure
articleSections.body: Manual: worn synchromesh (grinding), worn bearings (whining), worn selector forks (stiff shifting). Auto: burnt clutch packs (slipping), valve body wear (harsh shifts), mechatronic failure in DSG/DCT. CVT: belt or pulley wear. Diagnosis differs by type — choose a specialist for your gearbox.

articleSections.heading: Rebuild vs replacement vs used
articleSections.body: Rebuild: strip the gearbox, replace worn components — ideal for robust gearboxes like Toyota Hilux R151F. Exchange unit: professionally rebuilt, swap in, send yours as core — typically 1 day. Used low-km gearbox from scrapyard: cheapest (R3 000–R8 000) but carries unknown history risk.

articleSections.heading: When is a replacement cheaper than a rebuild?
articleSections.body: Some modern gearboxes are sealed units — BMW ZF 8HP, Mercedes 9G-Tronic. Labour costs R8 000–R15 000 alone. If internal hard parts are damaged, an exchange unit may work out cheaper. Your mechanic includes both options in the quote.

articleSections.heading: Gearbox oil: the most ignored maintenance
articleSections.body: Many manufacturers market lifetime transmission fluid meaning the expected gearbox life (150 000–200 000 km). Changing ATF every 60 000–80 000 km extends gearbox life dramatically in SA heat.

articleSections.heading: Average gearbox costs in SA (2026)
articleSections.body: Manual rebuild: R8 000–R18 000 (small cars), R12 000–R25 000 (SUVs). Auto rebuild: R15 000–R35 000. CVT: R18 000–R28 000. DSG mechatronic repair: R8 000–R18 000. Most Bouul mechanics include a 6–12 month warranty.

articleSections.heading: Can you prevent gearbox failure?
articleSections.body: Service gearbox oil at manufacturer intervals. Never hold a car on a hill with accelerator on automatics. In manuals, fully depress the clutch before each change. For DSG cars, use manual mode in traffic to prevent constant clutch slipping.

title: Engine Diagnostics: What the Warning Lights Really Mean
subtitle: That orange check engine light is not a suggestion — decode it before it costs you thousands
problemHeadline: Check engine light on? Do not ignore it.
problemBody: Modern cars have dozens of sensors. The check engine light could be a loose fuel cap or a failing catalytic converter. Many SA workshops charge R350–R800 just to plug in a scanner. With Bouul, the OBD-II scan is included and you get the report before authorising work.
bouulSolution: Your Bouul mechanic brings a professional-grade scanner reading manufacturer-specific codes from all ECUs
You receive a plain-language written report explaining each fault code, its severity, and cost estimate
Authorised repairs only happen after you approve — escrow holds payment until the warning light stays off
partsNeeded: Diagnostic scanner (Snap-on, Autel, or manufacturer-specific like VCDS, INPA)
Wiring diagram and repair manual for the specific vehicle
Replacement components per fault code diagnosis
Diagnostic printout and reset tool for clearing fault memory

aiPromptExample: 2016 Fortuner 2.8 GD-6. Check engine light came on driving to Polokwane. Engine feels normal, light is solid amber. Worried about DPF from short trips.
aiDiagnosisOutput: 2016 Fortuner 2.8 GD-6 — CEL solid amber. Likely DPF regeneration incomplete or O2 sensor. Est. diagnostic R500–R800. DPF regen R400–R800. O2 sensor R1 800–R3 500.
escrowGuarantee: After the diagnostic, you approve each repair. After the fix, escrow holds funds for 72 hours to confirm the light does not return.
pirbStandard: RMI Diagnostic Code of Practice; SANS 10100-2 for diagnostic equipment

articleSections.heading: Check engine light colours explained
articleSections.body: Solid amber: fault detected, driving may continue cautiously — book diagnosis within the week. Flashing amber: serious fault (usually misfire) that can damage the catalytic converter — stop driving. Red warning: stop immediately and call for assistance.

articleSections.heading: OBD-II scanners: generic vs professional
articleSections.body: A R300 Bluetooth dongle reads generic P0xxx codes only. Professional scanners (Snap-on, Autel, VCDS) read every ECU — transmission, ABS, airbag, body control — perform actuator tests, and show live sensor data including fuel trims and O2 voltage.

articleSections.heading: Common SA check engine light triggers
articleSections.body: Most common codes: P0171/P0174 (lean mixture — cracked hoses from heat), P0420 (catalyst efficiency — bad O2 sensor often), P0300 (random misfire — coil packs on VW TSI and Ford EcoBoost), P0401 (EGR insufficient flow — diesel bakkies on short trips).

articleSections.heading: Will disconnecting the battery reset the light?
articleSections.body: It clears the code temporarily but the fault remains. The ECU stores pending codes and the monitor runs through cold-start cycles before turning the light back on. You may get 50 km before it returns. If the fault is a misfire or lean condition, you are damaging your engine.

articleSections.heading: What happens during a professional diagnostic?
articleSections.body: The mechanic connects a scanner to the OBD-II port, reads fault codes across all modules, records freeze-frame data, and checks live data. They research severity against manufacturer bulletins and provide you a written assessment in plain English.

articleSections.heading: The Bouul diagnostic advantage
articleSections.body: Many SA workshops charge R350–R800 for the scan. With Bouul, the professional scan is included when you book a repair. The diagnostic fee is absorbed into the repair cost. Escrow means you never pay for a fix that does not work.
